### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleI18nRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7742278970ec0164a60d3bd306e28ad1ac515b2b` — the merge of head `2561fd5e28d735caf4367ec82a73cf68960c424c` into base `5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7742278970ec0164a60d3bd306e28ad1ac515b2b && git checkout 7742278970ec0164a60d3bd306e28ad1ac515b2b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351 2561fd5e28d735caf4367ec82a73cf68960c424c && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351 && git merge --no-ff 2561fd5e28d735caf4367ec82a73cf68960c424c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5c2e34cdb2b436f356ebba523e284e239f6ea351` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2561fd5e28d735caf4367ec82a73cf68960c424c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/i18n-supported-locales.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n-anonymous-deny.test.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx

Inputs read: card #36504 (body and all four comments, the claim 7120866660 and the os-dev-report 7123427766 included), PR #36858 (body, 28-file list, net diff against merge-base `f46ce5b4af`), and the check-runs on this head (63 success, 11 skipped, none failing or pending). The console files (`ui/packages/app-shell/**`, `ui/packages/i18n/**`) are the lane seat's remainder at its own tier; they were read here only to judge the declared deviations and the consumer of the new member.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`GetLocalesResponseSchema` gains optional `sourceLocale: z.string()`: a widening, right.** The body is a `z.object` (strips unknown keys), so the accept-set grows by one optional member and nothing that parsed before stops parsing. The input type `GetLocalesResponse` (re-exported by `@objectstack/client`, the return type of `client.i18n.getLocales` and of `ObjectStackProtocol.getLocales`) gains an optional member: no producer and no consumer breaks. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right declaration.
- **`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/GetLocalesResponse:sourceLocale` and nothing else: right.** One added row, matching the one added member; `Metadata-protocol: added` is the right kind.
- **Runtime accept-set: `GET /i18n/locales` body gains `sourceLocale` when the i18n provider reports a source or a default locale: right.** The value is `getSourceLocale?.()` else `getDefaultLocale?.()`, which is the collapse `II18nService.getSourceLocale` assigns to the caller (contracts/i18n-service.ts: the provider reports only what was declared). The member is omitted, not emitted empty, when neither is known, which is what the schema's description says. No other producer of this body exists: `toLocaleDescriptors` has this one call site, and service-i18n's ledger row is `disposition: 'sdk'`. The discovery document's `locale` block is a different shape and is untouched.
- **No narrowing anywhere in the diff.** The only removal is the UI string key `designMode.menu.renameSourceOnly` in the eleven `@object-ui/i18n` packs; its one reader (`DesignModeMenu.tsx`) is removed in the same diff, and `designMode.recordTabs.renameSourceOnly` (still read by `RecordTabsConfig.tsx`) is a different key and stays.
- **Console exports:** `fetchDefaultLocale` and `isSameLanguage` keep their signatures (`recordTabsConfigIo.tsx` still imports both); `rebaseMenuEdits` gains an optional fourth parameter; the save input type gains optional `labels`. All additive.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/36504-menu-rename-translation.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/runtime` patch, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, `@object-ui/i18n` patch. Every published package the diff touches is listed (`content/docs/**` is not a package). Spec minor is right for an added optional response member. The other three sit in the same `fixed` group as spec in `.changeset/config.json`, so they are released at the group's level whatever the line says; patch on them is not wrong.
- Clause-②: yes (widening) — on the PR body and in the changeset body, and it matches the diff.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is on both as well. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.
- **Deviation: `designModeMenuCreate.ts` outside the claim's file list — accepted.** One type line (`AppMenuSaveInput & { item }`) and the matching import. Without it the dashboard and report saves from the picker could not carry `labels`, and a label staged in a non-source language before 「New dashboard…」 would land in the stored label, which is the defect the card closes. It is the same save path the claim names, not a new surface.
- **Deviation: Done-when item 4 (object and field labels) — satisfied by its second arm; `Fixes #36504` is right.** The card's item reads "the same path serves object and field labels if the console later edits them, or a note says why not". The PR body gives the note, and it holds against the code: the console edits no object or field label in design mode, and those translations live under `objects.…` and are read by `translateObject`, not by the `apps.APP.navigation.ID.label` key `translateApp` reads (i18n-resolver.ts:2142). Items 1 to 3 and the thread's N5 (comment 7083013814) are each implemented and pinned. `Part of` would leave the card open with nothing left to build under it.
- **Deviation: two pushes while overlap-check exited 1 against #36848 — noted.** The overlap is textual, named in the PR body, and is the seat's to sequence; it changes nothing in this record's scope.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up #36873` — acceptable, and the right arm.** The rule (pm-dispatch SKILL.md:321) allows `skills/**` edits only on `domain:skills` PRs and sends every other PR to `follow-up #N`; this is a `domain:ui` PR. #36873 is open and names the file and lines. No skill text is made false: `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:387` names the route without its answer, and `:44` lists the tooling that reads the config key; neither says the server does not serve it. In `content/docs` the two hand-written route tables that list `/i18n/locales` are updated in this PR and `references/api/protocol.mdx` is regenerated; no page describes the old rename guard.
- **Security — the runtime change does not change who may read the endpoint.** `handleI18nRequest` still refuses an anonymous caller in its first statement, ahead of the service probe and of the `/locales` arm; the new lines sit below that gate. The `i18n-anonymous-deny.test.ts` hunk changes one literal, the body a signed-in caller is served on the locale-list face (it gains `sourceLocale: 'en'`); no deny assertion is touched. The new member is a deployment config value served on the same floor as the locale list beside it. `security_findings: none` agrees with the diff.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The runtime reads two in-memory accessors; the console reads one `translation` item by name through `/layers`.
- **Out-of-scope items the report lists with `carrier: none` — escalated to the seat.** (a) `RecordTabsConfig`'s tab-rename gate still compares the session with the default locale, the same gap this card closes for menus, and `sourceLocale` is now there to close it; (b) a source-language rename over an inline locale-map label replaces the map with a string. Neither is introduced here and neither blocks this head, but each needs a card or a stated reason before ACCEPT (filing-gate).
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` — holds.** Against the card: Done-when item 1 asks that `GET /i18n/locales` expose the source locale. A top-level `sourceLocale` beside `locales`, not an `isSource` mark on a row, is the right place: the declared source locale need not be one of the supported locales the rows list, so a row mark could have nothing to mark. `z.string()` matches the sibling `code`. Optional is right: a provider that implements neither accessor leaves the server with nothing true to say. The name follows the config key `i18n.sourceLocale`. The jsdoc's claims were checked against the code it cites: the collapse it describes is the one `II18nService` documents, and the first consumer (`fetchDeploymentLocales` in `designModeMenuSave.ts`) reads the member and falls back to the default locale when an older server omits it, so the member is optional on both ends.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts` — agrees with the contract.** It emits exactly what the schema describes. `i18n-supported-locales.test.ts` pins both arms through a real `AppPlugin`, memory i18n and the dispatcher, parsing the body with the schema itself; the dev's ablation of the spread turned that file red.
- **`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` — regenerated rows that match the member**; the generated-artefact gates are green on this head.
- **First consumer, read not reviewed:** the translation item the console writes (`name`, `locale`, `apps.APP.navigation.ID.label`) is a shape `TranslationItemSchema` accepts and the key `translateApp` reads, so the member has a consumer whose write resolves.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1: the changeset body still reads `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` while the PR body reads `follow-up #36873`. The changeset text becomes CHANGELOG text; point it at #36873 or drop the line there.
- N2: the Done-when item 4 note lives only in the PR body. One sentence in `designModeMenuSave.ts`'s module doc would keep the reason next to the code a later object-label editor would start from.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36504-menu-rename-translation`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzesUz1Y8VZuKJRhVL8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head 2561fd5e · 2026-11-24T06:05Z

L1 read of #36858 against card #36504. Head `2561fd5e28d735caf4367ec82a73cf68960c424c`; dev report 7123427766. Contract-review claim 7123487532. CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 record 7123562177: PASS, clean round.

**Face.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36858`: every item ok. All checks are now green at this head (Check Changeset was pending on the first read and has since passed); `mergeable_state` clean. `check-governed-merges.mjs` says NOT governed (0 of 28 paths; 995 changed lines). `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. `Skills-docs: follow-up #36873`: true. `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:387` names the endpoint, not its body, so no skill text is made false, and the two hand-written route tables in `content/docs` are updated here.

**Read and sound.**
- Server: `handleI18nRequest` answers `sourceLocale` = declared `i18n.sourceLocale`, else the default locale, and leaves it out when neither is known. The anonymous deny is still the handler's first statement, so who may read the endpoint is unchanged. The spec member is optional on a stripping object, with one `api.json` row. The changeset levels are right: spec minor; runtime, app-shell and i18n patch.
- Console: `splitLabelEdits` and `labelGoesToTranslation` send a label edit to the stored label only when the reader is in the source language and the entry is shown by its stored label. Every other edit becomes `labels` for `APP_menu_LOCALE` at `apps.APP.navigation.ID.label`, which is the key `translateApp` reads, and the entry keeps its served label. `writeMenuTranslation` reads the layered item and merges per id (a cleared name deletes it), then drafts with `ifNoneMatch: '*'`, then publishes with the publish pin. A refused publish resets the draft, and a pending draft is said in the new `translationPendingDraft` text. When the locales read fails, `labelLanguageOf` sets `source` to false, so the failure falls on the safe side: a translation, never an overwrite of the base label.
- Done-when items 1-3 are pinned (endpoint pin, zh-CN over English source with the English reader keeping the base label, guard relaxed). Item 4 is met by its "or a note says why not" arm, so `Fixes` is right.
- `designModeMenuCreate.ts` changes by one type line (`AppMenuSaveInput & { item }`) so that picker-created items carry the label language. This is a mechanical adjacent change outside the claim list, declared in the report; accepted.

**Changeset, read sentence by sentence.** Every sentence matches the diff except the declaration line noted in N1.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**Out of scope, for the seat (cards to file at landing; neither is touched by this diff).** These are the report's two `carrier: none` items, which the L2 escalated:
- (a) The `RecordTabsConfig` tab-rename gate (`recordTabsConfigIo.tsx`, `fetchDefaultLocale`) still compares the session language with the default locale. Now that `sourceLocale` is served, it can compare with the source locale instead. This is the same family as #36504.
- (b) A source-language rename over an inline locale-map label replaces the map with a string. The dev reports it as pre-existing and unchanged. The relaxed guard sends such an edit to the stored label only when the served label equals the stored one byte for byte.

Notes (nit, no action required):
- N1. The changeset's declaration line still reads `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`, while the PR body says `follow-up #36873`. The changeset text ships into the CHANGELOG, so `#36873` would read better there.
- N2. The Done-when item 4 note lives only in the PR body. One sentence in the `designModeMenuSave.ts` module doc would keep it next to the code.
- N3. `fetchDeploymentLocales` caches a failed read (`null`) for the rest of the page load. That is safe, since every rename then goes to a translation, but a source-language rename made after a transient failure lands in that locale's translation rather than the base label. Retrying on the next save would avoid it.
- N4. `isSameLanguage` matches a region-less tag to any region (`zh` = `zh-TW`). That is by design for `en`/`en-US`; recorded for a `zh`/`zh-TW` deployment.
- N5. The textual overlap with #36848 in `DesignModeMenu.tsx` and `designModeMenuCreate.ts` is known; whichever PR lands second rebases.
